# `m.options.contracts`

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

Reference data on options contracts: type, exercise style, expiration, and strike.

```python
m.options.contracts(symbols=None, *, underlying=None, contract_type=None, as_of=None, expired=False, sort=None, order=None, limit=None, filters=None)
```

## Plan access

Which of Massive's plans include this dataset, how recent its data is on each, and how far back its history goes, as Massive's pages state them.

| Options Basic | Updated daily, 2 years | Updated daily, 2 years |

| Options Business | Updated daily, All history | Updated daily, All history |

## Columns

| Column | Deephaven type | Description | Supplied by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Symbol` | String | The instrument, in the library's canonical symbol form. From REST `ticker`: "The ticker for the option contract." | REST |
| `OptionRoot` | String | The OCC option root, read from `Symbol`: the symbol without its `O:` prefix and its last 15 characters (expiry, type, and strike), such as `SPXW` for `O:SPXW251219C06000000`. It is never mapped to the underlying: an adjusted contract keeps its own root, such as `AAPL1`. | REST |
| `RawSymbol` | String | The symbol exactly as Massive sent it, on a row whose spelling the library cannot read as the dataset's class (its `Symbol` is then null); null on every other row. Present unless the session's `unreadable_symbols` is `dm.OnError.RAISE`, which fails on such a row instead. | REST |
| `AdditionalUnderlyings` | String | If an option contract has additional underlyings or deliverables associated with it, they will appear here. See here (https://www.optionseducation.org/referencelibrary/faq/splits-mergers-spinoffs-bankruptcies) for some examples of what might cause a contract to have additional underlyings. The column holds Massive's value as JSON text. | REST |
| `Cfi` | String | The 6 letter CFI code of the contract (defined in ISO 10962 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_10962)) | REST |
| `ContractType` | String | The type of contract. Can be "put", "call", or in some rare cases, "other". | REST |
| `Correction` | long | The correction number for this option contract. | REST |
| `ExerciseStyle` | String | The exercise style of this contract. See this link (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Option_style) for more details on exercise styles. | REST |
| `ExpirationDate` | String | The contract's expiration date in YYYY-MM-DD format. | REST |
| `PrimaryExchange` | String | The MIC code of the primary exchange that this contract is listed on. | REST |
| `SharesPerContract` | double | The number of shares per contract for this contract. | REST |
| `StrikePrice` | double | The strike price of the option contract. | REST |
| `Underlying` | String | The instrument Massive links the row to, exactly as Massive sends it; for an option, the linked instrument, not what the contract delivers. From REST `underlying_ticker`: "The underlying ticker that the option contract relates to." | REST |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, as an Instant: the local clock when the REST page, flat-file block, or WebSocket frame that carried it arrived, the same for every row of one. It is not monotonic and is not Massive's own receive time; on history() rows it is the download time, and in a poll() table the latest poll's. | REST |

`RawSymbol` holds Massive's spelling of a symbol the library cannot read; that row's `Symbol` is null, and `RawSymbol` is null on every other row. A session with `unreadable_symbols=dm.OnError.RAISE` (in code or in the settings file, as `unreadable_symbols: raise`) fails on such a row instead and has no `RawSymbol`; the table shows the default session.
